clue.text: Win back control, capturing Georgia

indicators.note: capturing says one piece holds another inside it, like a prisoner taken

parts.note: reins are what control a horse, so control can be REIN
GA is the standard abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

explanation.surface: A politician fights to regain control by winning the state of Georgia.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover something lost is to win it back.

clue.text: Religious education teacher lacking in attention

parts.note: RE is the school subject religious education
pupils address a female teacher as Miss

explanation.surface: A divinity teacher fails to keep the class's attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Being negligent means failing to pay proper attention.

clue.text: Man hides weapon inside item of clothing

indicators.note: hides says one piece conceals the other within itself

parts.note: a gent is a man
an arm is a weapon

explanation.surface: A man conceals a gun inside his coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A garment is any article of dress.

clue.text: Is priest unwelcome here?

parts.note: a lama is a Buddhist priest in Tibet
bad news is unwelcome

explanation.surface: A question about whether a clergyman would be shunned in a certain place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'here' is the definition: the place being asked about.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pakistani capital is the place the question points to, the 'here' of the clue.

clue.text: Fighting crushes a French soldier

indicators.note: fighting suggests a violent tumble, so the letters that follow are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: In battle, an enemy tramples a soldier from France.
explanation.definitionFit: A chasseur is a light infantry or cavalry soldier in the French army, from the word for hunter.

clue.text: Naval commander's speech in Cornish location, timeless

indicators.note: in says the speech goes inside the place name
timeless says T, the abbreviation for time, is removed

parts.note: Helston is a town in Cornwall, in south-west England
an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: An admiral gives an address in a Cornish town, losing track of time.
explanation.walkthrough: HELSTON is a town in Cornwall; 'timeless' drops its T to give HELSON, and 'in' puts ORATION inside after the H. The 's of 'commander's' stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's most famous admiral, victor at Trafalgar, was a naval commander.

clue.text: One captured by bird lover

indicators.note: captured by puts one piece inside the other that holds it

parts.note: a swan is a bird
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A man is caught by a bird-watcher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird lover' wants to be a birder, but 'lover' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Swain is an old poetic word for a young suitor or boyfriend.

clue.text: A ruler's weary after rising in African country

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the whole run is read from bottom to top

parts.note: ER is the Queen, Elizabeth Regina
to tire is to grow weary

explanation.surface: A monarch is exhausted after getting up in an African state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after rising' signals reading upwards, as this is a down clue; ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword ruler. The turned run gives AERTIRE read bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Eritrea is a nation on the Red Sea coast of north-east Africa.

clue.text: Fish with foul smell initially getting up one's nose

indicators.note: initially puts the smell word at the start, before the fish

parts.note: rank means smelly, having a foul smell
ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A stinking fish makes everyone recoil in disgust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' looks like a first-letter signal, but here it just places RANK first. 'Getting up one's nose' is British slang for annoying.
explanation.definitionFit: Something annoying or irritating gets up your nose; rankling means causing lasting irritation.

clue.text: Extra large fungus

parts.note: extra means additional, more
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: An oversized mushroom turns up.
explanation.definitionFit: The morel is an edible honeycomb-capped mushroom prized by cooks.

clue.text: Exclude evil Scotsman from Caribbean island

parts.note: to bar someone is to exclude them
bad means wicked, evil
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A wicked Scot should be kept out of a West Indian island.
explanation.definitionFit: A Barbadian is a native of Barbados, one of the Caribbean islands; the adjective means coming from there.

clue.text: Command soldier to follow black dog

indicators.note: to follow places the command and soldier after black

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
an order is a command
a terrier is a member of the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force

explanation.surface: An officer orders a soldier to trail a black dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The border terrier is a small rough-coated breed from the Scottish-English Borders.

clue.text: Boat to navigate round outer parts of Amsterdam

indicators.note: round says the steering word wraps around the other letters

parts.note: to steer is to navigate a vessel

indicators.note: the outer parts of a word are its first and last letters only

explanation.surface: A boat heads round the edges of Amsterdam, as on a canal tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' wraps the navigating verb around the city's outer letters; 'to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A steamer is a steam-powered ship or boat.

clue.text: Shoot a number on army exercise, say

indicators.note: say tells us the phrase before it is spoken, and the answer matches its sound

parts.note: a number is TEN, and an army exercise is a DRILL, so the phrase is 'ten drill'

explanation.surface: A soldier is told to fire a set number of rounds during a military exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoot' looks like firing a gun, but it is a plant's growth.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendril is a slender climbing growth from a plant, a kind of shoot.

clue.text: Rise of South Africa makes a nation tumble in struggle

indicators.note: something in a struggle is thrashed about, so the letters before are jumbled

explanation.surface: Unrest in South Africa makes the country fall during a political struggle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rise' is not an uprising but a physical height; 'in struggle' rearranges 'a nation tumble', with 'makes' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The flat-topped mountain overlooking Cape Town is a famous South African landmark, an elevation or rise.

clue.text: Film people other than you and me going round old port

indicators.note: going round says the people piece wraps around the rest

parts.words: people other than you and me
parts.note: people who are not you and me are not us
Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: A film about strangers on a journey round a historic harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitchcock's 1946 thriller starring Cary Grant and Ingrid Bergman is this movie.

clue.text: Vehicle's to act up when going through scrub

indicators.note: going through puts one piece in the middle of the other

parts.note: to scour is to scrub hard

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read upwards

explanation.surface: A car misbehaves as it bounces through scrubland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrub' looks like rough bushland but is a verb; 'up' turns the acting word to TCA, which 'going through' puts inside. The 's after 'Vehicle' means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A scout car is a fast lightly armoured military reconnaissance vehicle.

clue.text: He acted with troupe producing drama

indicators.note: producing suggests putting on a new show, so the letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An actor performed alongside a theatre company putting on a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'producing' rearranges HE ACTED plus TROUPE; 'with' simply joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: A coup de theatre is a sudden dramatic turn of events, a piece of theatrical drama.

clue.text: Spurn Tu moves for improvements to the economy?

indicators.note: moves says the letters shift into a new order

explanation.surface: A political figure called Tu rejects plans to boost the economy.
explanation.definitionFit: Upturns are rises or recoveries in economic activity; the question mark marks the definition by example.

clue.text: Land crumbling into sea

indicators.note: crumbling suggests falling apart, so the letters re-form in a new order

explanation.surface: Coastal land is eroding into the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Estonia is a Baltic country, a land in its own right.

clue.text: Girl taking part in archery lesson

indicators.note: taking part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A young woman joins an archery class.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheryl is a female first name.

clue.text: Speaker who stammers? No way

indicators.note: no says a piece is to be left out of the word before it

parts.note: one who stammers is a stutterer
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A stammering talker? Certainly not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No way' looks like an exclamation of disbelief; it actually says remove ST (street) from STUTTERER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who utters words aloud is a speaker.

clue.text: Land on lake in America

parts.note: re means on or about, as in business letters

indicators.note: in places the lake inside America

explanation.surface: A plane touches down on a lake in the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a kingdom or country, a land.

clue.text: Porridge will make righteous person vomit

parts.note: a saint, abbreviated ST, is a righteous person
to retch is to try to vomit

explanation.surface: A bowl of oats is so nasty it would make a saint sick.
explanation.walkthrough: PORRIDGE is British slang for time served in prison, as is a STRETCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British slang for a prison sentence.

clue.text: Pink Cadillac, perhaps, with lots of people at the back

indicators.note: at the back places the people after the car

parts.note: a Cadillac is one example of a car
a nation is a great many people

explanation.surface: A pink Cadillac drives with a crowd of fans following behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinks are a family of flowers including the carnation, which is a type of pink.

clue.text: I have rejected group of children worryingly

indicators.note: rejected says the hidden letters are read backwards
group of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A parent admits to having turned away a worrying gang of kids.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'I have', not just 'I': a possessor is someone who can say 'I have'. 'group of' hides RENWO in childREN WOrryingly, and 'rejected' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A possessor is the person who can claim to have something, so 'I have' is what such a person says.

clue.text: Increase speed in South Dakota location

parts.note: to rush is to speed
increase as a noun gives more

explanation.surface: A driver is told to go faster through South Dakota.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Increase speed' reads as an instruction, which RUSH MORE also is.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Rushmore, carved with four presidents' heads, is in South Dakota's Black Hills.

clue.text: Wife abandons Christmas revelry in storm

indicators.note: abandons says one piece walks out, leaving the rest

parts.note: wassail is festive drinking and carousing at Christmas

explanation.surface: A wife walks out on the festive party in a rage.
explanation.definitionFit: To storm a position is to attack it, to assail it.
